0.content:
In all of Liyue Harbor, the saying goes, only Beidou dares to bet against Ningguang. As Tianquan, Ningguang fines her again and again for smuggling and rule-breaking; Ningguang says the fines would buy a new ship, and once asked to have Beidou kept out of her sight. Privately she tried to reform her and gave up when Beidou called her deeds justice, charity and work for sailors. Rumour says Ningguang secretly runs the Crux. Ningguang says she hires Beidou, not the Crux; Beidou says they are equals and no one pulls her strings. Ningguang's advisers fear Beidou is a maverick; Ningguang calls her the most reliable person in Liyue, if you tell her the truth and what is in it for her.

They gamble and play chess (gossip says Beidou has won twice), and Beidou comes home tipsy promising to bankrupt her next time. Beidou did the hard work in Ningguang's 2.4 Jade Chamber plans and warned her about Beisht. In 2.5 (limited event) they vacationed in Mondstadt together, and Ningguang half-seriously accused her of poaching talent. Beidou admits she can never read the Tianquan's mind.

1.comment: Beidou: The Crux and the Alcor
1.content:
The Crux is an armed fleet based in Liyue Harbor, which Beidou established and leads. Its flagship, the Alcor, anchors off Guyun Stone Forest. It is famous for daring voyages and rich bounties and is very expensive to charter. It earns money as an armed carrier and through trade that is "not entirely above-board". After each long voyage the crew holds a three-day feast. The crew are fiercely loyal, and newcomers hear exaggerated tales of their captain that make her sound like a goddess.

Training splits recruits into the Shield of the Crux (survival: rescue, cartography, meteorology, medicine, counselling and entertainment) and the Spear of the Crux (naval warfare and cargo deals). Chief mate Juza trains newcomers. Surgeon Yinxing may send unfit recruits ashore and buys medicine at any price; the bookkeeper Mora-Grubber calls this a financial risk. Injured sailors draw support every year whatever the fleet's income. The fleet also runs a two-year navigation apprenticeship for the Ministry of Civil Affairs.

2.content:
Haishan was a vast dragon-like fish of the deep that every sailor was said to meet sooner or later. Liyue fishermen sang of it, and the song was Beidou's lullaby. She failed against it many times. In the final battle the fleet pinned it with cannon, harpoons, arrows and ropes for four days. Beidou fought it for ten hours, then waited all night at the prow, unfed, listening. At dawn she heard the waves change and took its head in one blow. Lightning struck the sea before her and an Electro Vision descended: a gift for the hero who subdued Haishan, as her character story puts it.

The tale spreads in exaggerated forms (a three-headed hydra cut through by a thrown sword), and Tea Master Liu Su tells it as "The Wrath of Haishan". Xiao, who has nothing to do with her, still acknowledges the feat. Her burst calls on "the power that ended Haishan".

3.content:
Beidou befriended the wandering samurai and, after he fled Inazuma under the Vision Hunt Decree with his dead friend's Vision, took him aboard the Alcor: "This guy's gonna be staying with us for a while. Take care of him, now." Even she did not realise at first how skilled a swordsman he was. In 1.6 he offered the Masterless Vision as the Crux Clash prize. She was wary of docking at Ritou with a wanted fugitive aboard.

After he blocked the Raiden Shogun's strike at Tenshukaku, he came back to the fleet and said he would sail a while longer; she was glad, and has promised to see him off with a drink whenever he leaves. He calls her a comrade every sailor can trust, and says she saved his life and gave him courage to return to Inazuma.

4.content: To save money on a three-day feast, the Crux lured a not-yet-famous Xiangling aboard. She warned Beidou she would not cook plain Yue-style seafood; Beidou offered fifty thousand Mora and told her to do what she was good at. Won over, Beidou told the crew Xiangling would soon be famous and ordered them to call her "Madam Xiangling". Xiangling now sails with them for exotic ingredients, admires Beidou's generosity and is surprised by how much she knows about seafood, though she does not always take Beidou's advice on what is edible. At sea the crew misses her fried jueyun chili most of all.

5.content:
Beidou had heard of the Traveler from Ningguang. When they came seeking passage to Inazuma she offered the Crux Clash prize as passage, and they won. She took them through the storm to Ritou in 2.0, telling them to give their all whatever "storms" they met, and was surprised to see them next at Tatarasuna with the resistance (2.1): "wherever you might end up, you'll always be part of Captain Beidou's crew." She would like them as a crewmate but will not tie them down, because she knows they have their own journey.

In her Hangout she stopped her crew pestering the Traveler to join, showed them the fleet's training and a staged smuggling run, and told them about Downriver. When the Traveler joked that they too might be cursed, since a Gnosis was taken after they reached each nation, she laughed and said that if anyone tries to make them a scapegoat, Captain Beidou demands to share the honour.

6.content: Downriver is an abandoned fishing village in Minlin, west of Wangshu Inn, founded by people from a place called Upriver. Beidou arrived at about five or six, chasing a dog that had stolen half a rice bun; the dog died with the bun still in its mouth, and she later said she would have let it keep the bun had she known. The village chief took her in. When he died and the catches failed, the villagers called her a curse and drove her out shouting "Nandou controls life! Beidou controls death!" Only then did she learn her name was a constellation and that its star Alcor meant death. Returning with the Traveler, she found only a few old houses still standing, among them the village chief's.

7.comment: Beidou: The Crux Clash and the voyage to Inazuma
7.content: In 1.6 Beidou held the Crux Clash on the Alcor, a Vision-less martial tournament with Kazuha's Masterless Vision as the prize. She added passage to Inazuma when the Traveler asked, moved them straight to the semi-finals, and was annoyed when the finalist failed to appear; he was the Treasure Hoarder Fei the Flyer, who had stolen the Vision. While Ningguang summoned her over the tournament, the Traveler was declared champion. In 2.0 she sailed through storms she blamed on the "Almighty Shogun", landed at Ritou, introduced Thoma as a trade partner, and left quickly with a fugitive aboard.

8.content: Kokomi hired Beidou's fleet and Kazuha as mercenaries. At the decisive skirmish their hidden reinforcements charged in at Kokomi's signal and Kujou Sara had to retreat; Beidou boasted that only the Alcor could ambush that quietly, and hoped Kokomi could afford all those mercenaries. Kokomi remembers doubting the ambush could stay hidden and Beidou proving her wrong, and would like her to train the Watatsumi fleet. Gorou respects that she keeps her companions out of disputes that are not theirs, so he asks only in dire need.

9.comment: Beidou: The Jade Chamber and Beisht
9.content: When Ningguang rebuilt the Jade Chamber (2.4), Beidou entered the materials contest with her new friend Yun Jin, consulted her chief smith Suling about Wonder Cores, and invited Shenhe to drink on her ship whatever happened. On launch day she arrived complaining she had been forced to help the Tianquan. Beisht, Osial's mate, then attacked; Ningguang had prepared because Beidou had warned her months before. The Crux fleet fought alongside the Millelith, Keqing and Ganyu.

10.comment: Beidou: Smuggling and the Ministry of Civil Affairs
10.content: In her Hangout Beidou showed the Traveler a "deal" arranged in fish-market code (bass heads, swim bladders, 81 scales) that ended with the Millelith inspecting innocent cargo at Guyun Stone Forest. It was a decoy: she and the Traveler are both on the Ministry of Civil Affairs' watch list, so their presence drew attention while the bookkeeper Mora-Grubber ran the real deal elsewhere. Beidou bears the Ministry no grudge; they are just doing their job.
